records.summary: A 350 mm cube enclosed CoreXY printer with a chamber heater that holds up to 60 °C and a 350 °C nozzle, sold in this version without the CFS color unit. It was $899 on 2026-11-18 against a $1,299 list price.
records.fit: Makers who want the largest build volume in Creality's K2 line for single-color ABS, ASA, nylon-CF or PPA-CF parts up to 350 mm (13.8 inches) a side. Buyers who already know they want multi-color should take the Combo: it adds one CFS for $200, less than the $299 the CFS costs alone. The QIDI Max4 ($1,049) does better on size and heat, with 390 × 390 × 340 mm, a 65 °C chamber and a 370 °C nozzle, and the QIDI Plus5 ($699) has the same 65 °C chamber in a smaller 320 × 320 × 300 mm volume.
caveats: Tom's Hardware found the bed needs about 15 minutes of heat soak before a large print gets a clean first layer.
Tom's Hardware could not get the closed chamber down to 30 °C and had a clog printing PLA with the door shut; Creality's own guide says to keep the chamber at 30 to 35 °C for PLA, PETG and TPU.

Owners on Creality's forum report extruder jams where filament bulges between the drive gears: one June 2025 buyer had two jams in the first three prints, and a December 2025 post describes a printer out of service for three months with an FR2836 feed error despite replacement parts.
It weighs 35 kg and measures 495 × 515 × 640 mm, so it needs a sturdy bench and two people to lift; 3DWithUs put the Combo's shipping weight at 54 kg.
Adding color later means buying a CFS, which per Creality's spec sheet does not feed flexible TPU, and HowToMechatronics measured 350 g of purge waste for 83 g of multicolor parts on this printer.

records.fit: Makers who want multi-color prints bigger than a 300 mm bed allows, such as helmets, props and batches of multicolor parts, and who also print ABS or ASA. The QIDI Max4 ($1,049) does better for single-color engineering work, with 390 × 390 × 340 mm, a 65 °C chamber and a 370 °C nozzle, though its QIDI Box color unit is a separate $228 purchase. The CFS does not feed flexible TPU, damp PVA or BVOH, or warped cardboard spools, per Creality's spec sheet; Tom's Hardware had TPU jam in the CFS tubing and printed it from the side spool holder instead.

Tom's Hardware found the CFS cables too short to stand the unit beside the printer, so it sits on the glass lid (916 mm tall in total) and has to be powered down and unplugged before the lid comes off.
3DWithUs hit a CFS retraction error and repeated tube-detached errors during testing, and owners on Creality's forum report extruder jams with filament bulging between the drive gears.

records.summary: A 300 mm cube enclosed CoreXY printer with a 60 °C heated chamber, bundled with one four-spool CFS for four-color printing and expandable to 16 colors. It was $749 on 2026-11-18 against a $1,099 list price; the same printer without the CFS was $549.
records.fit: Makers who want four-color printing plus ABS, ASA or polycarbonate capability in one enclosed machine, without the size and 35 kg weight of the K2 Plus. For single-color engineering parts the QIDI Plus5 ($699) does more for $50 less: a 65 °C chamber, a 370 °C nozzle and 320 × 320 × 300 mm, with no color unit at that price.

The long high-flow hotend purges a lot of filament at each color change, per Tom's Hardware, and Fabbaloo notes there is no purge bin in the box.

Owner reports on Creality's forum are mixed: one July 2026 poster had two units bought the month before both out of service with motion and CFS errors, while another reported about 3,000 hours with only occasional clogs.

records.summary: A compact enclosed CoreXY printer with a 300 °C steel-tipped nozzle for carbon-fiber-filled filaments, an AI camera and a 220 × 220 × 250 mm build volume. It has no chamber heater and was $499 on 2026-11-18.
records.fit: Buyers who need a small, 12.4 kg enclosed printer for PLA, PETG, TPU and carbon-fiber PLA on a desk 355 mm square. For ABS, ASA or nylon the K2 Pro without CFS ($549 on the same store) is the better pick, with a 300 mm cube volume and a 60 °C heated chamber for $50 more, and the QIDI Plus5 ($699) goes further with a 65 °C chamber and a 370 °C nozzle.
caveats: There is no chamber heater: Clever Creations needed 30 minutes to bring the chamber from 25 °C to its 38 °C maximum, and found a fan that cannot be switched off starts at that point.
Clever Creations found the carbon filter to be loose granules with wide gaps and noticed no difference in smell with it on or off, so ABS fumes are better vented outdoors.
Clever Creations found plastic extruder gears on its unit and had to partly take the print head apart to swap the nozzle, which is a Creality-only design.
Tom's Hardware notes the smooth PEI plate needs glue stick and the rear spool holder makes loading awkward; Creality supplies files for a printable side mount.
The 220 × 220 × 250 mm build volume is less than half that of a 300 mm cube printer, and color printing needs a separately sold upgrade kit.

records.summary: A 300 mm cube enclosed CoreXY printer with LiDAR first-layer scanning, an AI camera and a 300 °C nozzle, without a chamber heater. It was $549 on 2026-11-18 against an $899 list price.

notes: Price and stock: all five matched the brief. Each product page shows the given sale and list price in the visible text, in the embedded variant data (price and compareAtPrice) and in schema.org Offer markup with availability InStock; each shows Add To Cart and 'Estimated Shipping Date: Nov 18 - Nov 20'. No 'Sold Out' or 'Notify Me' on any of the five.
Item 3: the default variant on the K2 Pro page is 'K2 Pro Combo' at $749 (compare-at $1,099) and it is in stock (availableForSale true, InStock). The same page sells 'K2 Pro' without CFS at $549.
Unit counts in stock could not be verified: the embedded quantityAvailable numbers belong to bundle wrappers and could not be tied to a single variant with confidence.

Codes: no discount code is printed on the Creality US store today. Checked the banner, home page, 3D printers collection, the five product pages, /pages/black-friday-mega-sale, /pages/sale, /pages/student-discount and /pages/military-healthcare-first-responders-discount (reader copy and raw HTML). The store advertises codeless offers only: free shipping on all 3D printers, a '$500 coupon pack' for new subscribers (account sign-up, terms not shown), 6% off for verified students and a discount for healthcare, military and first responders (each issues a personal code by email after verification; the terms text on those two pages is rendered client-side and could not be read), bundle deals on /pages/sale, a 'Spend $300, get a free T-shirt' member-day gift dated Nov 15 to 17, and a 30-day price-difference promise printed on four of the five product pages (not on the K2 Plus printer-only page).

Not a store code: the creality.com K1 Max page (not the US store) contains leftover theme placeholder text reading 'The discount code has been applied to your cart, Code: CHPDISC6357X1' next to template filler copy. It is not presented as an offer, was not tested and should not be published.

K2 Plus weight conflict: creality.com's spec table and K2 series comparison say 35 kg (Tom's Hardware and 3DWithUs repeat 35 kg); the US store's /pages/compare page lists 32 kg. The records use 35 kg.

K2 Pro dimensions conflict: the store's spec table labels 445 x 505 x 850 mm as 'K2 Pro Dimensions', while creality.com and the store compare page give 445 x 477 x 573 mm for the printer. Tom's Hardware lists 445 x 505 x 850 mm as the Combo footprint, so the larger figure appears to be the printer with the CFS on top; Creality does not say so explicitly.
